title: spec review: S2b memory_scorecard and memory_eval: retrieval precision, downstream use, utility per token, and the P34 memory eval cases (P5, P34 memory)
spec:
Create orchestrator/memory_scorecard.py: read decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval and the bus outcome of their subject tasks. Per task: records_retrieved (candidates), records_presented (selected in active, legacy_ids in shadow), memory_tokens, downstream_use = share of presented records whose files or components appear in the task's changed paths (gitutil.changed_paths when a worktree exists, else the result's files list) or whose id/title words appear in the result summary, first_pass (merged without a fix round: no task with constraints.fix_round_for equal to it), fix_rounds count, repeated_retrieval (same record presented to the same lineage more than once), irrelevant = presented and not used. Aggregate per mode and per 7 days: precision (used/presented), utility_per_token (used records / memory_tokens * 1000), first_pass rate for tasks with memory vs without. CLI `orchestrator scorecard --memory [--days n] [--json]`. Create orchestrator/memory_eval.py with the P34 memory cases as deterministic checks over a temp root seeded from fixtures: current decision found in HOT, older decision found in WARM by search, historical provenance (superseded decision) found in COLD by search with tier cold, an irrelevant record excluded from a task's tiered sections, compaction preserves knowledge (every record still findable after compact). run(root) -> {cases: [{name, passed, detail}], passed, total}; persist to .orchestrator/memory_eval.json like context_eval does; CLI `orchestrator memory-eval [--json]`. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/08-memory-scorecard.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.

risks.issue: Spec says read decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval. T-1151 (the dependency) writes these rows with kind="retrieval" (orchestrator/spawn.py:811), and decision_log.py's CONTEXT_KINDS only contains "retrieval" — there is no memory_retrieval kind anywhere in the codebase. Implemented literally, the scorecard filters on a kind that never occurs and silently returns zero candidates/presented/tokens for every task.

downstream_use fallback is specified as "gitutil.changed_paths when a worktree exists, else the result's files list", but no task result in this repo ever sets a files key (zero hits for result.get("files") across orchestrator/ and tests/). The only guaranteed per-task file list is task.get("scope") (TaskCreated hook enforces it). Once a worktree is gone (the normal state after merge), changed_paths returns None and the fallback silently evaluates to an empty list, permanently biasing downstream_use/precision toward 0 for any merged task the scorecard evaluates later, e.g. the 7-day rollup.

memory_tokens source is unspecified while records_presented explicitly disambiguates by mode (selected in active, legacy_ids in shadow). The retrieval row's extra carries two different counts, tokens_legacy and tokens_tiered, that differ substantially by design (T-1151's own shadow-comparison table: 502 vs 236 tokens for one task). Without the same mode-conditional rule, utility_per_token becomes incomparable across modes depending on which count an executor picks.

suggested_spec_changes: Change 'decision_log rows of kind memory_retrieval' to 'decision_log rows of kind retrieval (T-1151's memory-retrieval evidence kind)'.

Change the downstream_use fallback to 'gitutil.changed_paths when a worktree exists, else task.get("scope")' — drop 'the result's files list', which has no corresponding field anywhere in the task/result schema.
Specify memory_tokens the same way as records_presented: extra.tokens_tiered for active-mode rows, extra.tokens_legacy for shadow-mode rows, so utility_per_token is computed consistently per mode.
